does: Parts the yolk of an egg from its white, so that each can be used alone: the yolks to enrich or thicken, the whites to whip.

intro.what: Separating eggs keeps yolks and whites apart for their different cooking roles.
intro.why: It teaches you to protect whites intended for whipping while reserving yolks for richness or thickening.

how: Set out a small bowl to separate over, and a larger bowl for the whites that are clean.
Crack the egg on a flat surface, not on a rim, and open it over the small bowl with the yolk in one half of the shell.
Pass the yolk gently from one half of the shell to the other until the white has run into the bowl.
Tip the yolk into its own bowl, and move the white to the larger bowl only when it is clean.

cues.text: The white is clear, with no streak of yellow in it, and the yolk is whole and round.

mistakes.mistake: Letting a speck of yolk fall into the whites, which then will not whip.
mistakes.fix: Separate each egg over a small bowl first, and lift out any speck with a piece of shell.

mistakes.mistake: Cracking the egg on the rim of a bowl, which pushes in shell and breaks the yolk.
mistakes.fix: Crack it on a flat surface.

quiz.question: Why separate eggs for different preparations?
choices: To use the whites for richness and the yolks as the only whipping part.
Yolks enrich or thicken while whites can be whipped.
To whip both parts together after checking their colour.
quiz.because: Each part has useful properties that a recipe may need independently.

quiz.question: Why separate each egg over a small bowl first?
choices: To mix any broken yolk into all the whites immediately.
To avoid needing a separate place for yolks.
To check the white before adding it to the collected whites.
quiz.because: An isolated egg can be checked without contaminating the whole bowl with yolk.

quiz.question: Which appearance suits whites intended for whipping?
choices: Whites with a broken yolk mixed through.
quiz.because: Yellow streaks indicate yolk contamination, which interferes with whipping the whites.

quiz.question: Cracking eggs on a bowl rim keeps breaking yolks. What should change?
choices: Strike harder against the sharp rim.
Crack them on a flat surface.
Open each egg directly into the collected whites.
quiz.because: A flat cracking surface reduces the rim pushing shell inward and damaging the yolk.
